newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges Farrakhan to raise Pan Am case in Libya.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges Farrakhan to raise Pan Am case in Libya.

text.p: The U.S. State Department on Monday called on American black Moslem leader Louis Farrakhan to raise during a visit he is making to Libya the case of an airliner allegedly sabotaged by Libyan agents.
"I just would hope that Louis Farrakhan would choose to raise the issue of Pan Am 103 with (Libyan leader Muammar) Gaddafi," department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
"I think Mr Farrakhan has a responsibility as an American, as a patriotic American, to raise that issue with Mr Gaddafi," Burns told a news briefing.
The United States alleged that two Libyan agents planted a bomb which destroyed the Pan Am airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland, in 1988, killing 270 people.
Libya has incurred U.N. sanctions by rejecting demands that it turn over the two men for trial in the United States or Britain.
After a previous visit by Farrakhan, leader of the Nation of Islam group, to Libya a year ago, the State Department blasted him for failing to raise the Pan Am affair.
The official Libyan news agency JANA reported on Monday Farrakhan had met Gaddafi and discussed with him the situation of blacks in the United States and the problems of Moslem countries.
Farrakhan, who arrived in Tripoli Sunday, last visited Libya in August 1996 when Tripoli awarded him a human rights prize worth $250,000.
But the U.S. Treasury Department denied Farrakhan's application to receive the money citing, among other reasons, the U.S. view that Libya was "a strong supporter of terrorist groups."
Farrakhan had said he wanted to use the money to build schools and business for blacks.
